title: Securing America's Defense Supply Chains and Domestic Acquisition of Critical Materials
summary: This executive order directs greater use of domestic and allied sources for critical materials and defense supply chains while addressing physical, cyber, economic, and foreign-dependence risks. It makes provenance, supplier security, and production capacity explicit acquisition concerns.
key_findings: Defense acquisition is directed toward more secure domestic and allied material sources.
Supply-chain security includes physical, cyber, economic, and foreign-control dimensions.
Critical materials are linked to defense production and the ability to sustain capability.
why_it_matters: It turns critical-mineral and supplier dependence into a procurement and industrial-base implementation question.
ftfn_relevance: Supports tracking origin, processing, supplier concentration, and acquisition rules.
Connects critical minerals with manufacturing, cyber risk, and national-security demand.
evidence_limits: The order directs implementation but does not prove that alternative suppliers or processing capacity exist.
Later acquisition rules, waivers, contracts, and capacity data are required to assess effects.
